question: All doctors are graduates. All graduates can read. Which conclusion must be true?
explanation: By transitivity: all doctors are graduates and all graduates can read, so all doctors can read.

question: No fish are mammals. All whales are mammals. Which must be true?
explanation: Whales are a subset of mammals; fish and mammals are disjoint sets; therefore no whale is a fish.

question: Some politicians are lawyers. All lawyers are well-read. Which conclusion definitely follows?
explanation: Politicians who are lawyers are also well-read, so at least some politicians are well-read.

question: All P are Q. No Q are R. Some R are S. Which conclusion is definitely FALSE?
explanation: All P are Q and no Q are R, so no P can be R. 'All P are R' directly contradicts this established fact.

question: If the power goes out, the alarm will not ring. The power went out. What must follow?
explanation: Modus ponens: Power-out → Alarm-silent. Power went out. Therefore alarm did not ring.

question: If Ahmed passes the exam, he will get a scholarship. Ahmed did not get a scholarship. What can we conclude?

options.B: Ahmed did not pass the exam
options.C: Ahmed will get a scholarship next year

explanation: Modus tollens: P→Q, ¬Q, therefore ¬P. Ahmed did not pass.

question: If it is Monday, the library is open. If the library is open, students can study. Today is Monday. What must be true?
explanation: Chain rule: Monday → library open → students can study. Since today is Monday, students can study.

question: At least one of Zara or Bilal must attend the meeting. Zara did not attend. What follows?
explanation: Inclusive disjunction: at least one must attend. Since Zara did not, Bilal must have.

question: Given: (1) If A then B. (2) If B then C. (3) If not-C then D. (4) D is false. Which statement must be true?
explanation: D is false. Contrapositive of (3): ¬D → C. Since D is false (¬D), C must be true.

question: Argument: Students who participate in extracurriculars perform better academically. Which statement most STRENGTHENS this?

options.A: Some extracurricular students have poor grades
options.B: A study of 10,000 students shows higher GPAs among those with extracurricular involvement
options.C: Extracurriculars reduce time available for studying
options.D: Not all successful students join activities

explanation: Large empirical data directly supporting the claimed relationship strengthens the argument.

question: Argument: The new traffic signal reduced accidents in City X. Therefore all cities should adopt it. Which most WEAKENS this?

options.A: City X saw a 30% drop in accidents
options.B: City X has unique traffic patterns not shared by any other city
options.C: Traffic engineers designed the system carefully
options.D: The mayor of City X endorsed the system

explanation: Unique conditions in City X mean results cannot be generalised, undercutting the universal recommendation.

question: Argument: Higher literacy rates correlate with lower crime. Therefore investing in education reduces crime. Which most STRENGTHENS this?

options.B: Longitudinal studies show communities receiving educational investment later report fewer crimes
options.C: Some low-literacy areas have low crime rates
options.D: Crime depends on many social factors

explanation: Longitudinal causal evidence (not mere correlation) directly supports the causal claim.

question: Argument: Company X's profits rose after switching to remote work, proving remote work increases productivity. Which most WEAKENS this?

options.B: Company X also launched a highly successful new product during the same period
options.D: Several other firms saw similar profit increases

explanation: A confounding variable (new product) explains the profit increase, severing the causal link to remote work.

question: Argument: People who exercise regularly live longer. Sara exercises daily. Therefore Sara will live a long life. Which most WEAKENS this?

options.B: Sara has a hereditary condition that significantly reduces life expectancy

explanation: A hereditary condition overriding exercise benefits undermines the specific conclusion about Sara.

question: A new medicine reduces fever in 90% of patients. Doctors should prescribe it for all fever patients. Which assumption does this argument make?

options.B: The medicine has no serious side effects
options.C: All patients want medication for fever
options.D: No other fever medicines currently exist

explanation: Broad prescription requires assuming safety; without this assumption, prescribing to everyone could cause harm.

question: Since smartphone usage increased, youth literacy has declined. The argument assumes which of the following?

options.A: Smartphones are used only by youth
options.B: Smartphone use causally contributes to declining literacy rather than merely correlating with it
options.C: Literacy was very high before smartphones

explanation: The argument moves from correlation to causation, which requires the assumption of a causal link.

question: We should invest in solar energy because fossil fuels will eventually run out. The argument assumes that:

options.A: Solar is the only alternative to fossil fuels
options.B: Solar energy is a viable and sufficient alternative for our energy needs
options.C: Fossil fuels will run out within ten years
options.D: Solar panels are inexpensive to manufacture

explanation: Recommending solar as the solution requires assuming it can actually meet our energy requirements.

question: A restaurant's revenues declined after a competitor opened nearby. The manager concluded competition caused the decline. This conclusion depends on which assumption?

options.B: No other factors such as economic conditions or menu changes contributed to the revenue drop

explanation: Attributing the decline solely to competition requires ruling out other possible causes.

question: A country's GDP grew 5% but most citizens feel financially worse off. Which best explains this paradox?

options.B: Almost all GDP growth went to the wealthiest 1% of the population
options.D: Welfare improvements always lag behind GDP growth

explanation: When growth is concentrated among the very wealthy, average citizens see no improvement despite overall GDP gains.

question: After introducing a disease-screening program, a hospital recorded more deaths from that disease even though treatment effectiveness was unchanged. Which best resolves this?

options.A: Screening caused the disease to spread
options.B: Screening detected previously undiagnosed cases, increasing recorded disease deaths without worsening survival rates
options.D: The disease became more prevalent because of screening

explanation: More diagnoses mean more deaths are attributed to the disease (previously unrecorded), not that treatment worsened.

question: After a workplace safety campaign, reported workplace accidents increased. Which best explains this paradox?

options.A: The campaign made workplaces more dangerous
options.B: Employees began reporting minor incidents they previously ignored
options.D: Companies hired more workers after the campaign

explanation: Greater awareness encourages reporting of previously unreported incidents, so more reports reflect a better reporting culture rather than more accidents.

question: Students who spend more time on homework consistently score lower on tests than those who spend less time. Which best resolves this paradox?

options.B: Weaker students spend more time on homework because the material is harder for them; ability drives time spent, not the reverse
options.C: Teachers assign too much homework to struggling students
options.D: Time on homework has no relationship to performance

explanation: This is reverse causation: low ability causes both more time needed and lower scores; more homework time does not cause lower scores.

question: Annual sales (Rs. millions): 2019: 120, 2020: 96, 2021: 108, 2022: 135, 2023: 162. What was the percentage increase in sales from 2022 to 2023?
School enrollment by grade: Grade 9: 240, Grade 10: 210, Grade 11: 180, Grade 12: 150. Grade 9 enrollment increases by 25% next year; all others stay the same. What will total enrollment be?
Test scores — Ali: 72, Sana: 85, Umar: 91, Nida: 68, Hamid: 84. The passing mark is 75. What percentage of students passed?
explanation: Students scoring ≥ 75: Sana (85), Umar (91), Hamid (84) = 3 out of 5 = 60%.

question: Monthly budget allocation: Rent 30%, Food 25%, Transport 15%, Education 20%, Misc 10%. Monthly income = Rs. 80,000. How much is spent on Education and Transport combined?
Factory quarterly output: Q1: 1,400 units, Q2: 1,600, Q3: 1,500, Q4: 1,800. Annual target was 6,000 units. By what percentage did actual production differ from the target?
explanation: Actual total = 1,400 + 1,600 + 1,500 + 1,800 = 6,300. Excess = 300. Percentage = (300 ÷ 6,000) × 100 = 5% above target.

question: Five friends A, B, C, D, E sit in a row. A is at the leftmost position. E is at the rightmost position. B is between A and C, and C is between B and D. What is the order from left to right?
explanation: A is leftmost. B is between A and C: A…B…C. C is between B and D: B…C…D. E is rightmost. Order: A B C D E.

question: In a row of 7 students, Raza is 3rd from the left. How many students are to his right?
explanation: Students to the right = 7 − 3 = 4.

question: Six books P, Q, R, S, T, U are on a shelf. P is at the leftmost position. T is immediately to the right of P. S is at the rightmost position. R is immediately to the left of S. Q is to the left of U among the two remaining positions. What is the order left to right?

options.A: P T Q U R S
options.B: P T U Q R S
options.C: P Q T U R S
options.D: P T R Q U S

explanation: Fixed positions: P(1st), T(2nd), R(5th), S(6th). Remaining spots 3 and 4 hold Q and U with Q to the left of U: Q(3rd), U(4th). Order: P T Q U R S.

question: Five people A, B, C, D, E queue at a counter. D is 2nd from the front. B is immediately behind D. A is at the back. C is immediately in front of A. What position is E in the queue?
explanation: D = 2nd, B = 3rd (immediately behind D), A = 5th (back), C = 4th (immediately in front of A). The only remaining position is 1st, so E is 1st.

question: A person is 4th from the left end and 6th from the right end of a row. How many people are in the row?
explanation: Total = (position from left) + (position from right) − 1 = 4 + 6 − 1 = 9.

question: Four friends A, B, C, D sit around a circular table facing the centre. A sits opposite C. B is immediately to the left of A. Who is immediately to the right of A?
explanation: In a 4-person circle with A opposite C, B is to A's left. The only person left (D) must be to A's right.

question: Six people A, B, C, D, E, F sit in a circle (positions 1–6 clockwise). A is directly opposite D (3 seats apart). C is 2 seats clockwise from A. Who is directly opposite C?
explanation: A at position 1, C at position 3 (2 clockwise from A). D is opposite A at position 4. Opposite of position 3 is position 3+3=6 = F.

question: Five people P, Q, R, S, T sit in a circle. P is 2nd to the right of R. Q is immediately to the left of P. S is 2nd to the left of T. T is immediately to the right of R. What is the clockwise order?
explanation: Place R at 1. T is immediately right of R: T at 2. P is 2nd right of R: P at 3. Q is immediately left of P (counterclockwise): Q at 2? Conflict with T. Re-interpret 'left' as clockwise position before: Q at 4 (the seat after P in anticlockwise reading). S is 2nd left of T: S at 5. Clockwise order: R(1) T(2) P(3) Q(4) S(5) — simplified as R T P Q S.

question: Eight people sit around a circular table. Amir is 3 seats clockwise from Sara. Bilal is directly opposite Sara. How many seats clockwise from Bilal is Amir?
explanation: Sara at seat 1, Amir at seat 4 (3 clockwise from Sara). Bilal is directly opposite Sara in an 8-person circle: seat 5. Going clockwise from Bilal(5) to Amir(4): 5→6→7→8→1→2→3→4 = 7 steps. Answer: 7.

question: Pointing to a man, Sara said, 'He is the son of my father's only daughter.' How is the man related to Sara?
explanation: Sara's father's only daughter is Sara herself. So the man is Sara's son.

question: A is the brother of B. B is the mother of C. D is the father of A. How is D related to C?
explanation: A and B share parents; D is A's father, so D is also B's father. B is C's mother, so D is C's maternal grandfather.

question: P is the son of Q. Q is the daughter of R. S is the husband of R. How is S related to P?
explanation: Q is R and S's daughter. P is Q's son. Therefore S (Q's father) is P's maternal grandfather.

question: Introducing a woman, a man said, 'Her mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the man related to the woman?
explanation: The man's mother's only daughter is the man's sister. The woman's mother is therefore the man's sister. The man is the woman's maternal uncle.

question: Raza walks 10 km North, then turns right and walks 5 km. In which direction is he from his starting point?
explanation: He moved North then East (right turn from North). His final position is North-East of the start.

question: Facing North, you turn 90° clockwise, then 180° anticlockwise. Which direction are you now facing?
explanation: North → 90° clockwise = East → 180° anticlockwise = West.

question: A man walks 6 km East and then 8 km North. What is the straight-line distance from his starting point?
Ayesha faces South. She turns 90° clockwise, then 45° anticlockwise. Which direction does she now face?
explanation: South → 90° clockwise = West → 45° anticlockwise from West moves toward South = South-West.

question: If CAT is coded as DBU (each letter shifted +1), how is DOG coded?
explanation: D+1=E, O+1=P, G+1=H → EPH.

question: If each letter is represented by its position in the alphabet, what does 16–5–14 decode to?
In a code, TRAIN is written as VTCKP (each letter shifted +2). How is PLANE coded?
explanation: P+2=R, L+2=N, A+2=C, N+2=P, E+2=G → RNCPG.

question: If MANGO = 50 (sum of alphabetical values: M=13, A=1, N=14, G=7, O=15), what is the value of GRAPE?
In a certain code, WATER is written as XBUFS (each letter shifted +1). STONE in the same code is written as?
explanation: S+1=T, T+1=U, O+1=P, N+1=O, E+1=F → TUPOF.

question: In a class of 30 students, Amir ranks 8th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
explanation: Rank from bottom = Total − Rank from top + 1 = 30 − 8 + 1 = 23.
